fichas.title: Miniature Golf: Course Rules and Equipment Standards
fichas.summary: Miniature-golf obstacles should differ both in appearance and in how they are played, while allowing a strategy. Borderlines mark the end of the first obstacle or the minimum tee-to-ball distance on lanes without built-in obstacles. Set-down markings are required where moving or setting down the ball is permitted. All lanes must be marked, and every lane should be reachable from the tee in one stroke. The page specifies target-hole limits, club-head area, and ball-diameter limits.

Cobigolf:
One of the most difficult lane systems, the 'little gates' set in front
of the obstacles are a special feature. The course also consists
of 18 lanes.These are in large format (12-14 m length) and also in
small format (6-7 m).
Sterngolf:
A Sterngolf course consists of 18 lanes; 17 of the concrete pistes
have a semi-circular target area and the last has a star as a 'target
circle'. This gives the system its name. The lane length is 8 m, lane
width 1 m and end circle diameter 2 m. The lanes are bounded by
pipes. The tee is marked by a circle of 30 em diameter and the
hole is 10 em diameter.

All the obstacles are standardised for all lane golf systems, and
selected and constructed according to sporting requirements.
Therefore it is possible to hole every lane in one stroke, because
every player of miniature golf aims to take as few strokes as
possible on every lane.

fichas.title: Miniature Golf Lane Designs and Standard Dimensions
fichas.summary: The page illustrates miniature-golf lane layouts, including a central circle, volcano, steep slope with V-obstacle, right angle, lightning flash, straight lane, sloping circle, circular plateau, and a run-up ramp with central opening. Some lanes are marked as playable only from the tee and without borderlines. The stated standard lane dimensions are length 6.25 m, width 0.90 m, and target-circle diameter 1.40 m.

fichas.title: Minigolf, Cobigolf, and Sterngolf Systems
fichas.summary: The page compares three lane-golf systems. Minigolf uses concrete pistes with tubular-steel frames and natural-stone obstacles. Cobigolf has 18 lanes in large or small formats, with little gates in front of obstacles. Sterngolf has 18 lanes, including 17 with semi-circular target areas and a final star-shaped target; its lanes are bounded by pipes, with a circular tee marking.
